articles.title: Ilia Topuria: "Lo que me mantiene motivado para 2027 es recuperar mi cinturón"
articles.standfirst: 'El Matador' está decidido a volver por todo lo alto tras su traspiés en el UFC Casa Blanca
articles.summary: 'El Matador' está decidido a volver por todo lo alto tras su traspiés en el UFC Casa Blanca
articles.body: Ilia Topuria ha dejado un legado imborrable en el mundo de las MMA y más concretamente en la UFC. En poco tiempo el peleador hispano georgiano se ha convertido en el primer doble campeón invicto de la historia de la compañía y ha dejado actuaciones para el recuerdo como los tres K.O. consecutivos a Alexander Volkanovski, Max Holloway y Charles Oliveira. Sin embargo, el pasado 14 de junio perdió el invicto y el cinturón de peso ligero en el UFC Casa Blanca ante Justin Gaethje, y ha afirmado que lo que le motiva a seguir es volver en 2027 pasa recuperarlo. Hace cinco meses, Ilia Topuria perdió su invicto y su corona en una noche fatídica en la que no le salieron las cosas, justo al contrario que a Gaethje. El peleador estadounidense realizó la estrategia perfecta y obligó a Aleksandre Topuria a parar la pelea antes de dar comienzo el quinto asalto, generando una espina se mantiene clavada en Ilia desde entonces. De hecho, una vez volvió a aparecer en el ojo público el pasado septiembre no ha parado de decir que su objetivo principal es una revancha inmediata con Gaethje, y en una entrevista con 'JD Sports' ha explicado su objetivo principal para 2027. "Lo que me mantiene motivado de cara a 2027 es recuperar mi cinturón. Quiero conseguir la revancha y volver a ser campeón", sentenció. Topuria tendrá el alta para volver a entrenar a alta intensidad y hacer sparrings a partir de enero, fecha en la que también se espera que se conozca más acerca de cuándo y contra quién peleará en su siguiente aparición. A pesar de sus intenciones, Gaethje no parece muy por la labor de darle una revancha, y la realidad es que un supercombate contra Paddy Pimblett está más cerca que nunca. De hecho, incluso 'El Matador' parece haberse cansado de llamar a la puerta de Gaethje, y a principios de semana puso un tuit donde retaba a Pimblett a realizar juntos 'The Ultimate Fighter' para luego medirse en el octágono. En caso de ganar a 'The Baddy', su archienemigo deportivo, tendría vía libre para volver a obtener una oportunidad titular y recuperar el oro. Topuria dijo hace unas semanas que pronto tendría reuniones con la UFC para negociar su siguiente pelea, así que todo debería esclarecerse pronto. Paddy Pimblett, Justin Gaethje o incluso Arman Tsarukyan por el cinturón vacante si Justin se retira son las opciones más viables, y todas ellas serían peleas muy mediáticas que en caso de ganar relanzarían la carrera de Ilia.

Ilia Topuria y Justin Gaethje, cara a cara. UFC.

articles.title: Daniel Dubois to fight Joseph Parker in WBO heavyweight world championship clash in Manchester on January 30
articles.summary: Daniel Dubois will box former world champion Joseph Parker on January 30 at Manchester's Co-op Live arena; Dubois will be defending the WBO heavyweight world title he secured defeating Fabio Wardley; Parker has had his suspension lifted
articles.body:
Dubois and Parker were due to box in 2025 for the IBF title, only for Dubois to fall ill and withdraw just three days before the fight.

Parker knocked out short-notice replacement Martin Bakole and then lost a WBO Interim title bout to Fabio Wardley.

In August he announced that he could continue his career after a suspension was lifted following a failed drug test in October 2025.

Dubois lost the IBF strap to Oleksandr Usyk last year but stormed back to form when he twice halted Wardley, winning and retaining the full WBO world championship .

He will now be back in action early in the new year against Parker, who's also recorded standout wins over Deontay Wilder and Zhilei Zhang in recent years.

A former holder of the belt, the New Zealander lost the WBO championship to Anthony Joshua back in 2018 at the Principality Stadium when he became the first professional opponent to go the distance with Joshua.

Frank Warren said: "This heavyweight showdown will deliver a blockbuster beginning to 2027.

"It's a fight everyone wanted to see, and I'm thrilled we can now make it happen. Daniel is entering his prime and when he is on his game it is hard to picture anybody beating him.

"But Joseph has long promised to become world champion again, and now he gets his chance. "

images.caption: Image: Daniel Dubois will fight Joseph Parker next in Manchester on January 30

articles.title: Daniel Dubois to defend heavyweight title against ex-Anthony Joshua rival in Manchester
articles.summary: Daniel Dubois has beaten domestic rival Fabio Wardley twice in 2026 and now has his next opponent lined up
articles.body:
Daniel Dubois will put his WBO heavyweight title on the line against former champion Joseph Parker at Manchester's Co-op Live Arena on 30 January.

The pair were previously scheduled to fight for the IBF belt in 2025, but the contest was called off days before when Dubois fell ill.

Dubois claimed the WBO belt by beating domestic rival Fabio Wardley at the venue in May, before repeating the win inside two rounds in a London rematch in October.

Parker previously held the WBO crown between 2016 and 2018 before losing to Anthony Joshua in a unification fight, and he has not boxed since an interim title loss to Wardley in October 2025.

Promoter Frank Warren said: "Daniel is in his prime and when he is on his game it is hard to picture anybody beating him.

"But Joseph has long promised to become world champion again, and now he gets his chance."

Parker has not fought in 2026 after he tested positive for cocaine shortly before his defeat by Wardley, although the result of the test was only made public after the stoppage loss.

The New Zealander maintained his innocence following the positive test and was cleared to fight in August following an investigation.

"I'm pleased to confirm my provisional suspension is lifted, and I'll be back in the ring soon," Parker said in August, per the BBC.

"I've been advised to say no more for now while details are finalised. Thank you to all my supporters."

Parker has a professional record of 36-4 (24 KOs). His other defeats came against British duo Dillian Whyte and Joe Joyce. However, he does hold impressive wins over Deontay Wilder, Derek Chisora and Martin Bakole.

Wilder and Bakole are due to fight each other on the undercard of Joshua's highly-anticipated clash with Tyson Fury in Cardiff next month.

images.caption: Dubois will face Joseph Parker in January (Steven Paston/PA Wire)

articles.title: Fury v Joshua: Joe Cordina to face Mexico's Mauricio Lara
articles.summary: Joe Cordina will face former world champion Mauricio Lara on the undercard of Tyson Fury versus Anthony Joshua in Cardiff next month.
articles.body:
Joe Cordina will face former world champion Mauricio Lara on the undercard of Tyson Fury versus Anthony Joshua in Cardiff next month.

Mexican Lara rose to prominence by beating Josh Warrington in a huge upset in 2021 and claimed the WBA featherweight title from Leigh Wood in February 2023.

Wood won back his title later that year and in 2025 Lara was banned for two years for an anti-doping violation, which backdated to March 2024.

The 28-year-old has fought twice since returning from his ban earlier this year, beating compatriots Rafael Rosas Ramirez and Carlos Ornelas.

Fury vs Joshua fight to go ahead despite objections over 3am finish

Wilder to fight Bakole on Fury-Joshua undercard

Confirmation of Cordina's bout against Lara now completes the undercard of the all-British contest between Fury and Joshua at the Principality Stadium on 11 December.

Cordina, 34, the former IBF super-featherweight champion, had wanted to face all-time great Manny Pacquiao, 47, in his home city.

The Welshman had agreed terms to face the Filipino legend - who has not fought since July 2025 - but Pacquiao did not reciprocate.

Pacquiao, a 12-time world champion across eight different weights, may also have settled on facing an opponent in early 2027 instead.

articles.title: AEW Dynamite Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights From November 25
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of AEW Dynamite on November 25.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of AEW Dynamite on November 25.

In the U.S., this is Thanksgiving week, so AEW put together a great card with more action from the Continental Classic. Here is a look at what was advertised for Wednesday's show:

Wrathlander vs. Divine Dominion (Women's Tag Team Championships)

Let's take a look at what happened on the Thanksgiving Eve episode of Dynamite.

The first match of the night was another C2 bout. Cassidy and Bailey fought for another three points in the tournament.

These are two babyfaces who have never had a single issue, so this was as clean as a match can get. There was no funny business, no attempts to take shortcuts, and no heel tactics.

Wrestling is built on the battle between good and evil, but sometimes, it's refreshing to watch two grapplers just do what they do best without having to worry about one of them looking like a bad guy.

Speedball and OC are both gifted performers. They have slightly different styles, but both men are capable of working at a quick pace and using high-flying moves, so they have more than enough in common to put on a fun show for the crowd.

This was a strong performance from both guys, even with a couple of small missteps along the way. The C2 is known for producing some of the best matches in AEW, and these continued that reputation.

They traded several near-falls before Bailey countered the Orange Punch with a spin kick for the win.

Daniel Garcia being injured and forced to drop out of the C2 is very unfortunate. He is being replaced by Konosuke Takeshita.

OC got a near-fall that he and the crowd thought should have been a three-count. It was pretty questionable.

Speedball's springboard moonsault looked good on his end, but OC wasn't in the best position to take it and had to fall even though he barely got hit.

The way Bailey uses kicks is so unique compared to most. He employs martial arts techniques better than a lot of people.

The next match was another in the ongoing C2 tournament. This time, it was Knight and Moxley who fought for the next three points.

This is one of the bigger mismatches in the tournament. Knight is the young high-flyer looking to make his mark, and Moxley is the wily veteran who prefers violence over technique.

However, these kinds of matches might not usually happen outside of this tournament. It's fun to get these unique combos of opponents, especially when one is a rising star and one is a decorated former world champion.

The vast difference in their styles meant we got sequences designed to highlight them separately. Moxley was finding ways to ground The Jet, and Knight kept trying to find shortcuts and use his aerial ability to his advantage.

The pace was a little slower than expected at first, but they did that to play some mind games, and it led to some entertaining exchanges and moments. However, it also led to the match being a little less exciting than we know these two can be.

The final couple of minutes were the best part. Mox did a great job making it look like Knight might get the victory before he eventually got a submission with an armbar.

It's a little weird that Knight is the only one of the 10 members of the Don Callis Family in this match.

The rules of the tournament forbid anyone else from being at ringside, so Marina Shafir and Don Callis had to stay backstage.

Knight sold the piledriver like he was sent to another dimension.

The next match featured two teams of nine facing off. The entirety of The Don Callis Family, minus Knight and Kyle Fletcher, faced a bunch of enhancement talents.

This was not just a squash match. It was the squashiest squash to ever squash. The jobbers didn't get in a single shred of offense. This was basically just an exhibition for the DCF to show off.

Josh Alexander got the win for the DCF with an ankle lock. This barely qualified as a match. It was probably fun for the live crowd, but it didn't really serve a purpose.

Swerve Strickland, Kofi and Austin Creed came out on the stage to taunt them after the match.

Brody King has the look of a vicious heel, but the personality of a pure babyface. His backstage interview with Hangman and Bandido was quick but good.

Creed had some mic issues when he started talking. So did Kofi, but it was a completely different issue.

Rhodes vs. Punk Will Be Epic, More Raw Fallout 🔥

Mercedes Mone appeared with The Cut before the match and issued a challenge to AZM for a match after what happened last week. Everyone else had to leave once Hangman came out because this was another C2 matchup.

White played some mind games by giving Hangman a hug before they got started. These two know each other well and are both former members of The Bullet Club, so this was an interesting bout on multiple levels.

There wasn't a lot of technical wrestling in the early minutes of the match. They were mainly throwing punches and chops, and it made it feel like a hard-hitting affair right out of the gate.

They kept a steady pace, increasing in some spots to build momentum, and slowing down so they could do it again. By the time the announcers said 10 minutes had passed in the allotted 20, it felt like both men were just hitting their stride.

The combination of solid in-ring work and storytelling made this an enjoyable match, even if it felt like they were holding back and could have gone much harder. White pulled out the win with a Blade Runner after Page almost beat him with the exact same move.

White giving Mone a bunch of nicknames to use for their intro was hilarious.

White wearing a cowboy hat is probably an insult to Hangman on some level.

Hangman hit some nasty chops. White sold them perfectly.

They appeared to mess up a powerbomb spot, but they reset and hit it on the second try.

The only title match on the card saw Harley Cameron and Kris Statlander defend the women's tag titles against Megan Bayne and Lena Kross.

We've seen these women fight each other before, so we knew what to expect. Statlander matched up against the power of Bayne and Kross while Cameron played the underdog against Divine Dominion.

Bayne accidentally took out Kross with a diving clothesline when Cameron moved out of the way, and it felt like that was the turning point.

The action in this match was good, but it felt like pacing was their issue. They didn't take much time to sell big moves because they wanted to pack in as much as possible, but it wasn't a huge factor.

Statlander pinned Kross to retain the titles after Cameron took out Bayne with a backstabber. The losers attacked the champions after it was over and posed with the belts until Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor showed up to fight them off.

Result: Wrathlander defeated Divine Dominion

The Brawling Birds, who just lost the titles, gave an interview saying they are coming for the winners.

Go watch one of Cameron's first matches and compare it to this and you will see massive growth in a couple of years.

Statlander's running crossbody against the ropes looked good. She almost threw herself right out of the ring because she hit it so hard.

MJF came out and gave a promo where he challenged Will Ospreay to a title match again. Ospreay issued a pre-recorded response. It was revealed that they will have a Ladder match at Worlds End.

When El Idolo came out for his match against Fletcher, MJF finally left the ring, but he said he would not leave the stage until his bout with Ospreay was changed to a normal match. Fletcher came out and had a staredown with him before he decided to leave.

Andrade had the edge in experience, but in every other way, these two felt like an even match for each other. They were even going move for move at one point, with neither man able to gain a clear advantage.

Putting this match in the main event spot was smart because it ended up being the best thing on the show. They gave us a match that had just the right amount of selling while still having the perfect pacing.

Callis tried to give Fletcher his screwdriver, but El Idolo got ahold of it. After a momentary distraction, The Protostar hit his finisher to get the win. This was a great match with an ending that made sense for both men.

MJF said the show was over in his promo right at the time the show was actually scheduled to end.

Fletcher has been planting seeds for a babyface turn, and the crowd is already responding.

The exchange of chops was loud and looked brutal. They were not holding back.

Andrade pulling off a few moves while his pants were around his ankles was impressive and creative.

Wednesday's episode of Dynamite only had one weak point with the 18-man tag match, but even that offered a little bit of fun.

The Continental Classic continued to deliver great matches, and three we got this week all stood out for completely different reasons.

The women's tag title bout was decent, but the match that stole the show was Fletcher vs. El Idolo. Neither of them have had a single bad match in 2026, and they were not about to break that streak tonight.

Fletcher is continuing to gain popularity, and AEW needs to strike while the iron is hot. If it waits too long, his eventual babyface turn will not have the same impact.

articles.title: Israel Adesanya Reveals Unity MMA Setup, Opens Up About Difficult Split With City Kickboxing After 16 Years
articles.summary: Ahead of his UFC Saudi Arabia outing against Shara Magomedov, Israel Adesanya talks about moving on from City Kickboxing.
articles.body:
UFC Saudi Arabia is scheduled for December 5 at the ANB Arena in Riyadh, with Israel Adesanya set to headline against Shara Magomedov . For Adesanya, the matchup could be one of the most important fights of his career as he looks to snap a four-fight losing streak.

However, the event also marks a new chapter for Adesanya outside the Octagon. It will be his first UFC appearance since parting ways with his longtime gym, City Kickboxing, and head coach Eugene Bareman in July earlier this year.

Now, the former 185-pound champion has opened up about his decision to leave his longtime camp while also offering a glimpse into his new training setup. Adesanya is now preparing for his return at Unity MMA, working with a smaller team that includes some familiar faces from his previous camp.

Speaking on his YouTube channel , the former champion explained how his new coaching team came together. He said, "I just decided to stick with what I had, and I have Andrei Paulet, who was my wrestling coach at CKB, but he's way more than a wrestling coach; that's just his foundation."

He added, "And I have 'Twist' (Tristam) Apikotoa and just through Andrei, I trusted him and he was able to help me and guide us in the right direction because he knows me. He brought in Twist because Twist has always been there, too."

Adesanya further explained how his training camp eventually found a home at Unity MMA. "And then, I picked two guys to help me with this camp initially, and then Twist brought in sparring partners from South Auckland. And now Unity MMA, which is perfect, just up the road from us. It was them that gave us a home because I was looking around the area."

The 24-6 former champion also addressed his decision to leave City Kickboxing after spending nearly 16 years with the New Zealand-based gym. Adesanya admitted that walking away from the team was an emotionally difficult experience. "It was a hard decision, and I would describe it like it could have been worse than a breakup. You've had bad breakups."

He elaborated on how his perspective on relationships and long-term commitments changed as he got older. "And then sometimes when I was younger, I could feel like, man, I've spent so much time with this person, I've invested this much, I don't want to lose all those years. And then you stick to it regardless of the disrespect, the manipulation."

Adesanya further explained why he eventually decided to move on rather than remain committed to a situation he no longer felt comfortable with.

He said, "But you stick with them because it's like you don't want to let those [years] go to waste. But then, as I got older, I can see things for what they are. So, as hard as it was, it also was really easy once I got it done. Once I ripped the Band-Aid off, I was like, 'Oh, I can see the forest for the trees,' so it was good."

Ultimately, Adesanya revealed that he trusted his instincts and refused to let anyone else cloud his judgment . After nearly 16 years with CKB, the former champion is now entering a new phase of his career with a different coaching setup.

His upcoming clash with Magomedov will offer the first glimpse of how the changes have translated inside the Octagon. With four consecutive defeats behind him, Adesanya will be desperate to get back to winning ways when he headlines UFC Saudi Arabia on December 5.

articles.title: We now have an official Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua ring walk time for boxing fight
articles.summary: Here's what you need to know about Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua, including when the two fighters should make their way to the ring.
articles.body:
It took a while for Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua to face off for a fight years in the making. Now, we are one step closer to seeing the two clash on December 11.

There was plenty of debate about where the fight would take place, from New York, Saudi Arabia, to the U.K. Those in charge of the fight, now in Wales, prefer it to air at a time that an American audience can see.

That request could result in U.K. fight fans being excited and exhausted by the end of the event. For a fair time, there needed to be approval from local authorities, Cardiff Council's licensing sub-committee, South Wales Police and the Welsh Rugby Union.

Here's what you need to know about Fury vs. Joshua, including when the two fighters should make their way to the ring.

Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua main event start time

Main event start time (approx.): 8:30 p.m. ET | 5 p.m. PT | 1:30 p.m. GMT

Location: Principality Stadium - Cardiff, Wales

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are expected to walk to the ring around 8 p.m. ET. The main event should begin around 8:30 p.m. ET (1:30 p.m. GMT).

The event must be over by 3 a.m. GMT (10 p.m. ET) as Principality Stadium closes at 3:30 a.m. GMT.

Fight fans are advised to be at the stadium by 11:30 p.m. GMT.

In the Middle East, the main event should start by (on Dec. 12):

articles.title: ‘My Back Against The Wall’ – Kongklai Eyes Statement Rebound Against Worapon At The Inner Circle 40
articles.summary: The Thai star sounds off before his crucial bout against his compatriot.
articles.body:
Long before he reached the global stage, Kongklai Sor Sommai had already mastered the art of the comeback. He lost the first 10 bouts of his career, then rattled off 18 straight wins.

Back-to-back defeats are hardly the deepest hole he has climbed out of, and his next turnaround begins against fellow Thai Worapon Lukjaoporongtom in the bantamweight Muay Thai co-main event of The Inner Circle 40 on Friday, November 27. The card goes down live in Asia primetime from Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium, exclusively for members at live.onefc.com .

Not long ago, the former Omnoi Stadium Champion looked as lethal as ever. Stoppages of Ferrari Fairtex and Mohammad "Prince of Persia" Habibpour bookended a hard-fought win over Kendu Irving , giving him three consecutive victories and his best run in ONE.

Then came a pair of painful setbacks. Julio Lobo outpointed him at The Inner Circle 12 in May, before Adam "El Capitano" Benwarwar survived two knockdowns to stop him in the second round at The Inner Circle 22 in July.

Looking back on both losses, Kongklai admits his eagerness to entertain sometimes got the better of him. In the weeks since, he has worked to close the gaps in his armor.

"For this camp, my team focused extra attention on my defense because my opponent is also a southpaw with a dangerous high kick. "I keep reminding myself not to get careless or repeat the same mistakes. I have to protect myself properly and not get dropped by a single clean shot."

"I keep reminding myself not to get careless or repeat the same mistakes. I have to protect myself properly and not get dropped by a single clean shot."

Shoring up his own game is one thing. Exploiting Worapon's is another, and Kongklai believes Lenny Blasi has already shown the way. At The Inner Circle 28 , the Italian swarmed Worapon with a high-tempo attack to snap his 3-0 run in 2026.

Now, he intends to borrow a page from that playbook.

"Worapon's signature weapons are his high kick, strong inside clinch work, and dangerous sneaky elbows. As for his weaknesses, he doesn't seem to like tricky, persistent pressure. In his recent loss to Lenny, when he faced fast pressure, he couldn't get his range and lost his focus. "I've prepared a game plan for that too, though if he chooses to brawl head-on, I'm ready to match him right from the start."

Still, Kongklai isn't expecting the same Worapon that Blasi faced. This time, he meets a fellow southpaw with a matching appetite for exchanges, and neither man has ever been content to coast.

Look closer, though, and the resemblance has its limits, at least in his eyes.

"My advantage over Worapon is my reach. I'm slightly taller, which makes it harder for him to close the distance. "I think this fight comes down to physical toughness because we're both aggressive fighters. Whoever has better stamina and timing will take the win."

For Kongklai Sor Sommai, the equation is simple. A win over Worapon Lukjaoporongtom would keep his hopes of a US$100,000 main roster deal alive, while another loss would make that path considerably steeper.

Thailand's 2020 Fighter of the Year has stared down far longer odds, and he is treating this one with the urgency of a man who refuses to slide any further.

"This fight feels like a must-win situation, so I'm fighting with my back against the wall. There's no backing up, just trading head-on and bringing out my best form. "Losing three straight at the end of the year wouldn't be good. Most importantly, let's make it an exciting fight. Winning and losing are part of the sport, and the fans get the real treat."

Above all, Kongklai has built his reputation on never short-changing a crowd. Cautious, feel-out affairs hold little appeal, and fans craving edge-of-your-seat drama know exactly where to find him.

It is a standard he plans to uphold at Lumpinee, and one he wants Worapon to hear loud and clear.

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua loser will have nowhere to go, says Duke McKenzie | 'Moses Itauma will come again'
articles.summary: Former three-weight world champion Duke McKenzie believes whoever loses the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight will have to retire; McKenzie worries that Joshua's changes of trainer will be detrimental; He believes Moses Itauma can still come back and take over as a new star heavyweight
articles.body:
Fury vs Joshua is a major event. It will fill a stadium, at 1am in Wales, and command a no doubt huge broadcast audience in Britain and across the world.

But it is happening a late stage for both. McKenzie thinks whoever's defeated in the fight would have to retire from competition.

"There's nowhere to go for the loser. Either of them, whoever loses, it's their career finished. And even for the winner he's going to be one fight away from retirement," he told Sky Sports .

"Let's hope that none of these boys get hurt, they both go home with their health and their wealth and they can live their lives."

Since losing to Andy Ruiz, in a shock upset in 2019, Joshua has brought in multiple difference trainers to his corner, most recently leaving Igor Golub, of Oleksandr Usyk's team, to return to Ben Davison for this fight.

McKenzie thinks he's still looking for something.

"Since [the Ruiz loss] he's had this coach, that coach, he doesn't know what time of day it is in terms of where he actually fits and what suits him. Five, six, seven years ago this happened and there's miles on the clock now with AJ," McKenzie said.

"That's what a defeat can do to you. When you lose for the first time in your career it robs you of something which you never get back. Once that '0' goes very few get it back. Unfortunately for AJ that's where he finds himself."

Fury and Joshua have been major stars in world boxing and British sport. But McKenzie does see a candidate waiting to fill the void when they do retire.

"Moses Itauma. He will be the next big thing in world boxing. What's happened to him [losing to Filip Hrgovic], it's like a wake-up call for him really," McKenzie said.

"He wasn't putting in the work, that was obvious. I think it's easy to get drunk on all the pats on the back that you're getting. Everywhere he turned, everyone was telling him how great he was because he was blowing people away and making it look easy. It's easy to get drunk on that sort of adulation.

"I don't think I've known a world champion, past or present, that hasn't had a shocker or had a fight before they'd won a world title that they should have won but they looked shocking in, or indeed they've lost it.

articles.title: McGregor anuncia su regreso: "La rodilla está a punto y el cuerpo a pleno rendimiento"
articles.standfirst: Tras sufrir una grave lesión en el ligamento cruzado el pasado julio, 'The Notorious' ya está preparado para cerrar su combate de despedida con la UFC en 2027
articles.summary: Tras sufrir una grave lesión en el ligamento cruzado el pasado julio, 'The Notorious' ya está preparado para cerrar su combate de despedida con la UFC en 2027
articles.body: El pasado 11 de julio, Conor McGregor se volvió a subir al octágono cinco años después para medirse a Max Holloway en el combate estelar del UFC 329. Sin embargo, a los tres segundos de comenzar la pelea lanzó una patada y sufrió una grave lesión en el ligamento cruzado de su pierna derecha que le ha obligado a parar durante varios meses. 'The Notorious' tiene pendiente una pelea más en su contrato con la UFC, y en las últimas horas ha confirmado que ya está de vuelta para despedirse por todo lo alto y así redimirse de unos últimos años de carrera bastante aciagos para sus intereses. Tras convertirse en el primer doble campeón simultáneo de la compañía en 2016, Conor se pasó al boxeo para realizar un supercombate con Floyd Mayweather, lo que fue el inicio del fin para su carrera en las MMA. En su regreso a la UFC en 2018 fue sometido por Khabib Nurmagomedov, y desde entonces ha sumado tres derrotas y una victoria. Fue noqueado por primera vez en la compañía en su revancha contra Dustin Poirier, y en la trilogía en 2021 se fracturó el peroné. Cinco años después volvió para enfrentarse a Holloway después de varios escándalos extradeportivos, y el final fue aún más cruel para él. A pesar de haber sufrido dos graves lesiones de manera consecutiva, McGregor no se ha rendido en su intento de despedirse como se debe de la UFC, y después de operarse ya está pensando en su vuelta en 2027. "La rodilla está a punto y el cuerpo está a pleno rendimiento. Me estoy preparando para el campamento", afirmó McGregor en un vídeo compartido en sus redes sociales. Después de años en los que era noticia por su vida personal más que por sus éxitos deportivos, en 2026 Conor se había centrado y no había parado de entrenar para dejar atrás sus fantasmas del pasado. Es cierto que la mala suerte le vino a visitar ante Holloway, pero está más motivado que nunca. Se ha tomado muy en serio la recuperación, está quemando plazos a un ritmo vertiginoso y ya está con la mente puesta en su siguiente objetivo. En el vídeo que ha compartido se le ve entrenando en la bicicleta, haciendo ejercicios de gimnasio e incluso realizando ejercicios de manoplas, aunque todavía no está pateando. Se espera que aún necesite algunos meses para volver a estar al 100%, y teniendo en cuenta que es la mayor superestrella de la historia de la UFC lo normal es que su combate de despedida sea en verano, en la International Fight Week. Conor ha dicho que no tiene pensado renovar con la compañía, ya que quiere probar nuevos retos, por lo que será un 'The Last Dance' a una de las carreras más emblemáticas de los deportes de contacto. 'The Notorious' quiere cerrar la trilogía con Holloway a toda costa para redimirse de su último combate, pero todavía está por ver qué nombres le pondrán sobre la mesa Dana White y su equipo.

articles.title: El ICE libera al excampeón mundial Jorge Linares tras 10 días detenido en Estados Unidos
articles.standfirst: El venezolano se retiró del boxeo profesional en 2023, tiene "autorización" para vivir en EE.UU. y ha "cooperado completamente" con las autoridades migratorias
articles.summary: El venezolano se retiró del boxeo profesional en 2023, tiene "autorización" para vivir en EE.UU. y ha "cooperado completamente" con las autoridades migratorias
articles.body: El excampeón mundial venezolano de boxeo Jorge Linares quedó libre tras permanecer detenido durante diez días por el Servicio de Inmigración y Aduanas de Estados Unidos (ICE, en inglés), según difundió el propio deportista este jueves. "De vuelta a casa!! Gracias a Dios, a mi esposa y a todos mis familiares, amigos y fans por sus oraciones y apoyo!! No hay mejor regalo que regresar a casa en Thanksgiving! (Día de Acción de Gracias) Infinitamente agradecido", escribió Linares -en sus historias de Instagram- al compartir una imagen con su pareja. Horas antes, el presidente de la Asociación Mundial de Boxeo (WBA, en inglés), Gilberto Mendoza, había reportado la liberación del venezolano, quien el 15 de noviembre denunció -en X- que el ICE lo había detenido en El Paso, estado de Texas, ciudad fronteriza con México. "Excelentes noticias. Nuestro amigo y excampeón mundial AMB Jorge Linares ya está de vuelta con su familia! Gracias a todos por su apoyo, y un agradecimiento especial al abogado Richard Wilner y a su equipo. ¡Bienvenido, campeón!", publicó Mendoza -en X-. El venezolano, quien se retiró del boxeo profesional en 2023, tiene "autorización" para vivir en EE.UU. y ha "cooperado completamente" con las autoridades migratorias, según expuso días antes la firma de abogados Wilner O' Reilly, encargada de su defensa, en un comunicado compartido con EFE. Los defensores no entregaron más detalles sobre el estatus migratorio o la situación de la detención de Linares "por respeto a la privacidad y al proceso legal", mientras el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) no detalló el caso. Linares, originario de Barinitas, en el noroeste de Venezuela, es considerado uno de los boxeadores más exitosos de su generación y obtuvo los títulos de campeón mundial en los pesos pluma, superpluma y ligero.

images.caption: Fotografía de archivo del 26 de mayo de 2005 del boxeador venezolano Jorge Linares celebrando tras adjudicarse el titulo Fedecentro Pluma de la AMB en Buenos Aires (Argentina). EFE

articles.title: Evalúan la salud mental de Tyson Fury tras afirmar que es esquizofrénico y peligra la pelea con Joshua
articles.standfirst: La Junta Británica de Control de Boxeo estudia el caso de 'Gypsy King' antes de declararlo apto para su gran pelea del 11 diciembre en Cardiff
articles.summary: La Junta Británica de Control de Boxeo estudia el caso de 'Gypsy King' antes de declararlo apto para su gran pelea del 11 diciembre en Cardiff
articles.body: El combate entre Tyson Fury y Anthony Joshua es una de esas peleas de las que se lleva hablando años y, cuando por fin ha salido adelante, ha surgido un contratiempo que se la podría llevar por delante. El caso es que el ‘Rey Gitano’ reveló que le diagnosticaron “esquizofrenia leve” al hablar abiertamente sobre sus problemas de salud mental en un nuevo documental de Netflix. Dicho diagnóstico podría cambiar el tramo final de la carrera del excampeón mundial, comenzando por el devenir de su duelo con AJ, que cuenta con una bolsa de 150 millones de dólares. Según informa el Daily Mail, la Junta Británica de Control de Boxeo (BBBofC por sus siglas en inglés) está estudiando los informes médicos que indican que el ‘Gypsy King’ padece esquizofrenia y trastorno bipolar antes de dar luz verde a su combate por el título mundial de peso pesado contra Joshua en el Principality Stadium (Cardiff) el próximo 11 de diciembre. Robert Smith, secretario general de la BBBofC, ha sido tajante en lo relativo a este caso: “A Tyson no se le permitirá subir al ring a menos que nuestros médicos estén convencidos de que no existe riesgo para su salud. Estamos revisando toda la información sobre su estado mental y tomaremos una decisión sobre la autorización del combate en los próximos días”. Recordemos que Fury lleva peleando en estas condiciones desde hace más de una década, pues según relató le diagnosticaron la esquizofrenia poco después de ganar el título mundial contra Wladimir Klitschko en 2015. Precisamente nunca se llegó a disputar la revancha de aquella pelea, que incluso contó con dos fechas, pues el inglés fue declarado "médicamente no apto para pelear" y de hecho se anunció que no estaría disponible “en un futuro próximo”. Justo después de aquella cancelación arrojó un resultado positivo -por cocaína- en un control antidopaje de la AMA. El púgil de Mánchester reconoció posteriormente sus problemas de salud mental y adicciones. El ‘Rey Gitano’ logró levantarse de la lona para convertirse posteriormente en uno de los grandes campeones de peso pesado de las últimas décadas y todo ello pese a las enfermedades mentales que lo acompañan. “No hay palabras para explicar la oscuridad en la que me encontraba. Era como la versión real de las profundidades del fuego del infierno”, afirma el británico en el citado documental de Netflix, y añade a este respecto: “Estaba convencido al cien por cien de que acabaría en una habitación acolchada con la puerta cerrada con llave, y eso me daba muchísimo miedo”. ‘Gypsy King’ contó que en 2016 sufrió un ataque de ansiedad y acudió al hospital. Como resultado de aquello visitó a una psiquiatra en Londres, fue sometido a una serie de pruebas y “marcaron todas las casillas. Depresión, ansiedad, trastorno bipolar”.

images.caption: Tyson Fury y Anthony Joshua durante la presentación de su combate. Rasid Necati Aslim / Getty Images

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Paris Fury clarifies fighter did not have schizophrenia diagnosis
articles.summary: Paris Fury, the wife of Tyson Fury, says the boxer has never received a diagnosis of schizophrenia.
articles.body:
Paris Fury, the wife of Tyson Fury, says the boxer has never received a diagnosis of schizophrenia.

In clips promoting the release of a forthcoming Netflix documentary, the heavyweight fighter spoke of his mental health struggles in the months after he beat Wladimir Klitschko to become world champion in 2015.

He detailed hearing voices in his head, while wife Paris said he had "mild schizophrenia" .

Netflix has now edited the film ahead of its release on Friday, 27 November.

In a statement, Paris Fury said: "I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary.

"I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson's condition and I used the word 'schizophrenic'. While Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn't have this condition and has never received a diagnosis."

She added: "Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love. I'm so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we've received as a family."

A spokesperson for Netflix told BBC Sport: "Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson's official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch."

It comes after the British Boxing Board of Control said it was looking into Tyson Fury's comments about his schizophrenia diagnosis but was "fairly confident" the British heavyweight will be cleared to fight Anthony Joshua next month.

Fury, 38, is due to face Joshua at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December, with the ringwalk expected in the early hours of 12 December.

"We are in the process of dealing with the matter but if there are any medical issues we wouldn't let anyone box - it doesn't matter if it's Tyson Fury or not, it could be anybody," Robert Smith, the board's general secretary, told BBC Sport.

"I'm fairly confident he will be absolutely fine. We're dealing with it now and we'll have an answer very shortly."

Under regulation 8.1(b) of the British Boxing Board of Control's 2026 rules and regulations , external , schizophrenia is among the conditions that "may preclude" a boxer from obtaining a first licence, while for an existing licence holder the board "may take such action as in its absolute discretion it sees fit".

Smith would not say what the process would involve over the next few days, saying "it's a medical matter".

He said all boxers on the card will undergo medical checks, adding: "If our doctors are satisfied he's fit to box, he will box."

Originally, the documentary featured the Furys recalling his admission to hospital in June 2016 with a suspected heart attack.

Doctors said he had suffered an anxiety attack. He was diagnosed with schizophrenia after he left hospital, according to the film.

The NHS describes schizophrenia as a form of psychosis, and symptoms can include hallucinations, delusions and muddled thoughts and speech.

"Words can't explain the darkness I was in," Fury said.

The heavyweight, who struggled with drug and alcohol addiction after beating Klitschko, says a Halloween night out in 2017 prompted him to return to training, calling that a "turning point" after being "embarrassed by how I looked".

He went on to beat Deontay Wilder in 2020 to become world heavyweight champion for a second time.

Fury vs Joshua fight to go ahead despite objections over 3am finish

articles.title: Ilia Topuria, de nuevo en Miami para entrenar con uno de los mejores entrenadores de boxeo de la historia
articles.standfirst: 'El Matador' ha puesto a punto su striking con Pedro Díaz
articles.summary: 'El Matador' ha puesto a punto su striking con Pedro Díaz
articles.body: Ilia Topuria ya está de vuelta en el gimnasio preparando su regreso tras su derrota ante Justin Gaethje en el UFC Casa Blanca. Después de unos meses apartado del foco mediático y centrado en recuperarse de sus lesiones, 'El Matador' ha regresado a Miami y se le ha visto puliendo su striking junto a Pedro Díaz, uno de los mejores entrenadores de boxeo de la historia. Pedro Díaz es sinónimo de éxito en el mundo del boxeo. En su etapa en la selección cubana fue partícipe directo en los oros olímpicos de boxeadores como Félix Savón, Joel Casamayor, Héctor Vinent, Guillermo Rigondeaux, Odlanier Solís o Yuriorkis Gamboa. Además, también fue entrenador de la selección de República Dominicana y le dio el primer oro olímpico al país en boxeo con Félix Díaz. Por si fuera poco, en el ámbito profesional también ha entrenado a púgiles de la talla de Miguel Cotto. Por este mismo motivo, Topuria ha decidido entrenar junto a él para sumar sus conocimientos a los de Javi Climent, entrenador habitual de striking de Ilia. El propio Pedro Díaz ha subido una foto juntos a Instagram, junto con un bonito mensaje. "Esa mano en mi hombro era mucho más fuerte en los guantes. Buenas rondas hoy". Como el propio Topuria anunció recientemente, a partir de enero 'El Matador' ya podrá volver a entrenar MMA con normalidad una vez reciba el alta médica tras sus fracturas de ambos orbitales, la nariz y el pie. Sin embargo, ya está afilando sus habilidades en el boxeo para regresar en plena forma en 2027. Ilia ha dicho que en las próximas semanas espera reunirse con la UFC para negociar su siguiente combate, aunque la idea de un enfrentamiento contra Paddy Pimblett cada vez cobra más fuerza. Justin Gaethje no quiere darle una revancha inmediata e incluso existe la posibilidad de que se retire, por lo que 'The Baddy' es la mejor opción a nivel competitivo y mediático.

images.caption: Ilia Topuria entrenando junto a Pedro Díaz. Instagram
Ilia Topuria, tras ganar a Charles Oliveira. UFC.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua undercard: Martin Bakole insists late-notice Deontay Wilder fight won't be like Joseph Parker loss
articles.summary: In his first interview since agreeing to step in to fight Deontay Wilder, Martin Bakole explains his decision and why he believes this late-notice assignment will be very different from when he flew in to fight Joseph Parker; Bakole says victory will lead him to a world title shot
articles.body:
After Jai Opetaia withdrew from his December 11 bout with former heavyweight world champion Wilder, Bakole came in to take his place on the Principality Stadium bill.

He insists it is a very different scenario to his short-notice assignment against Joseph Parker last year.

Bakole came in to box Parker for the WBO Interim title, landing in Riyadh just a day before the fight. Parker promptly put him down heavily and stopped him in their second round.

For this fight with Wilder though he's had more warning. He was training in Las Vegas to box on the same bill, albeit originally for a much lower-level opponent.

"When I heard Wilder doesn't have an opponent, his opponent cancelled, they proposed me and I said why not? I'm ready to give a big fight," Bakole told Sky Sports . "Why not jump from a comeback fight to a big fight?

"I was surprised they mentioned my name and I said yes," he added. "I'm ready to come back again because I want to take over now the heavyweight division.

"I don't see Deontay beating me. He doesn't have the strength I have.

"I don't see any danger because I like danger, I like to impose myself.

That wasn't the case for Parker when he took that fight. "I was out in the Congo on holiday, I jumped in," Bakole said.

"In that fight I was giving Joseph Parker a hard time in the first round but because I was not fit and my head was not moving, he landed a punch. But I don't regret that fight. It's just part of my story.

While Bakole has been training in Las Vegas, he will still have long-time coach Billy Nelson in his corner for the fight.

"I came here to learn something new. I was getting ready for everyone," Bakole said. "Everything has changed [with his preparation], conditioning, nutrition."

He believes victory over Wilder will lead him to a world title shot next year.

"Of course," Bakole said. "That's why I wanted to change everything because I know next year, with my team, with His Excellency's [Saudi financier Turki Alalshikh] help, I will get a world title next year."

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Paris Fury retracts claim her husband has been diagnosed with schizophrenia
articles.summary: Paris Fury says Tyson did not receive a diagnosis of schizophrenia; Netflix documentary has now been updated; The British Boxing Board of Control indicated it would look into comments about a schizophrenia diagnosis and could deny Fury a licence to face Anthony Joshua on December 11
articles.body:
A new Netflix documentary explores Tyson Fury's experiences of depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder, which became particularly acute after his unified heavyweight championship victory over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.

Paris Fury made the comments about schizophrenia in an initial version of the documentary. Netflix said it has worked to "update" the footage in light of her clarification.

She has now said: "I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson's condition and I used the word 'schizophrenic'. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn't have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.

"Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love. I'm so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we've received as a family."

Earlier on Thursday, the British Boxing Board of Control (BBBoC) indicated that it was investigating the comments and could deny Fury a licence to face Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11 if he was deemed unfit to fight.

Sky Sports News has contacted the BBBoC to clarify if an investigation is ongoing after Paris Fury's retraction.

A spokesperson for Netflix said: "Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson's official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch."

After his victory over Klitschko, Fury revealed he had struggled with drug and alcohol addiction and had gained weight.

He was admitted to hospital in June 2016 with a suspected heart attack, and revealed that while in hospital he had heard voices in his head.

"Words can't explain the darkness I was in," Fury said during the Netflix documentary.

"It was like a living version of the pits of hell.

"I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.

"The anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it and that's when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London. She asked me a gazillion questions, and I ticked all the boxes. Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder."

The NHS says schizophrenia is a long-term mental health illness that is a form of psychosis.

Those suffering from the condition may, at times, be unable to distinguish their own thoughts from reality. Symptoms can include hallucinations and delusions.

The NHS describes bipolar disorder as a mental health issue where a person can experience extreme changes in their mood.

If you've been affected by anything discussed in this article, support is available; please visit Sky Viewer Support .

If you are worried about your mental health, get advice and support through your GP or call the NHS on 111.

Find free, confidential support through:

Samaritans: Call 116 123 (available 24/7)

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: How heavyweight rivals changed British boxing forever
articles.summary: Before their long-awaited heavyweight bout, BBC Sport explores the impact Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have had on British boxing.
articles.body:
They have conquered the world, filled stadiums and transformed British boxing.

Now, after more than a decade of lingering tension and endless debate, Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are finally preparing to share a ring.

They are from different worlds, with contrasting personalities and wildly different journeys to the summit of heavyweight boxing.

Fury is the unpredictable showman who dethroned a seemingly unbeatable champion. Joshua is the Olympic golden boy who became a global superstar.

Who is better? Who has achieved more? The arguments have raged in pubs, boxing gyms and across social media.

We may soon get our answer, but whatever happens when the first bell sounds in Cardiff in the early hours of 12 December, their greatest achievement may already be secure.

Together, Joshua and Fury have taken British heavyweight boxing to new heights, attracting wider audiences and inspiring the next generation.

How Fury and Joshua brought big-time heavyweight boxing to Britain

Britain had produced heavyweight champions before, but for years many of the division's biggest fights took place overseas.

Lennox Lewis fought some of his defining bouts in Las Vegas and Memphis. Challengers travelled to Germany when the Klitschko brothers reigned.

In November 2015, Fury outpointed Wladimir Klitschko in Dusseldorf. Less than five months later, Joshua knocked out Charles Martin at London's O2 Arena to win his first world title in his 16th professional fight.

"Bosh, that's it. The revolution starts in that six-month period," said BBC Radio 5 Live boxing pundit Steve Bunce, who was interviewed for the BBC documentary Rivals: Fury v Joshua.

Joshua's former trainer Rob McCracken saw an early sign of his appeal in Birmingham, where a show sold out with Joshua on the undercard.

"I'm from Birmingham, and it's hard to get a big crowd that sort of size," McCracken says. Promoters soon realised Joshua was bringing in a different audience and could sell tickets almost instantly.

By 2017, Joshua was fighting in front of 90,000 fans at Wembley Stadium, where he stopped Klitschko, while Fury's trilogy with Deontay Wilder made him a box-office draw in the USA.

"The two of them have been in eight massive stadium fights over an eight-year period," Bunce says. "That's reshaping British boxing history."

Yet for all the domestic ground they broke, both men eventually helped export the division's biggest nights back overseas - trading British stadiums for Saudi Arabian paydays, with even this Cardiff homecoming bankrolled by Turki Alalshikh's 'Riyadh Season' and timed for an American streaming audience.

Crossover stars who inspired the next crop of heavyweights

Fury and Joshua's reach extended beyond boxing. Joshua became a familiar face on chat shows, while Fury stepped into a WWE ring and welcomed Netflix cameras into his home.

Derek Chisora, who lost three times to Fury, could see that wider appeal in the crowd on fight night.

"You've got a guy who's running a hedge fund for £2.5bn having a drink with a guy who works for the local council," Chisora says.

Crossover contests - both faced former UFC champion Francis Ngannou, while Joshua fought YouTuber Jake Paul - reflected a sport increasingly blending competition with entertainment. But a lot of boxing fans viewed those fights as lucrative, low-risk detours that stalled the division.

Even so, that mainstream visibility turned Fury and Joshua into household names - and sustains Britain as a major centre of the division for another generation.

Today, a new wave of British heavyweights - Daniel Dubois, Fabio Wardley and Moses Itauma - are stepping into a landscape Joshua and Fury helped create.

Seven years after Joshua stopped Klitschko at Wembley, Dubois beat Joshua on the same ground. "Two legends of the sport," Dubois says. "What they've done for the sport in the last few years has been great."

Highly rated British prospect Leo Atang was 10 when he watched Joshua beat Klitschko on television at home in York and decided to give boxing a go. Seven years later, he won gold at the World Under-19 Championships.

Wardley remembers Fury's win in Dusseldorf as the night that "re-sparked a lot of people's love for boxing".

Yet for all Fury and Joshua have achieved, one question has followed them both throughout their careers is: what would happen if they met in the ring?

After failed negotiations, lost titles and shifting circumstances, some believe their bout is arriving too late. Chisora describes it as "getting the last drink in the barrel".

For years, promotional politics, rival broadcast deals, and mutual risk aversion kept both camps protecting their commercial brands rather than risking undefeated records.

In the time it took to make the fight, both men lost twice to Oleksandr Usyk and Joshua was beaten by Andy Ruiz Jr and Dubois.

Fury's father John Fury did not even want the fight to take place.

"Both men are bigger than boxing, both men [are] bigger than the event. Leave them, they're both multi-millionaires. They don't need to fight," he says.

But former world champion Natasha Jonas believes legacy ultimately comes down to what fighters feel they have achieved.

"Legacies are a huge thing. Once you walk away, you want to be happy and satisfied with what you've done and what you've left behind," she says.

The reality is that - barring a late withdrawal - Fury and Joshua will put their reputations on the line in front of 80,000 fans in Cardiff.

But, whether their rivalry is settled in 12 rounds or a single punch, Fury and Joshua's wider legacy has been built over more than a decade of filling stadiums, drawing new audiences and making British heavyweight boxing a global attraction.

images.caption: Image caption, Tyson Fury (left) has 36 wins, two defeats and one draw as a professional, while Anthony Joshua has 30 wins and four defeats

After failed negotiations, lost titles and shifting circumstances, some believe their bout is arriving too late. Chisora describes it as "getting the last drink in the barrel".

For years, promotional politics, rival broadcast deals, and mutual risk aversion kept both camps protecting their commercial brands rather than risking undefeated records.

In the time it took to make the fight, both men lost twice to Oleksandr Usyk and Joshua was beaten by Andy Ruiz Jr and Dubois.

Fury's father John Fury did not even want the fight to take place.

"Both men are bigger than boxing, both men [are] bigger than the event. Leave them, they're both multi-millionaires. They don't need to fight," he says.

But former world champion Natasha Jonas believes legacy ultimately comes down to what fighters feel they have achieved.

"Legacies are a huge thing. Once you walk away, you want to be happy and satisfied with what you've done and what you've left behind," she says.

The reality is that - barring a late withdrawal - Fury and Joshua will put their reputations on the line in front of 80,000 fans in Cardiff.

But, whether their rivalry is settled in 12 rounds or a single punch, Fury and Joshua's wider legacy has been built over more than a decade of filling stadiums, drawing new audiences and making British heavyweight boxing a global attraction.
